COMMUNITY BLOG · EATING OUT

How I stopped ordering “the usual”

🌻Aisha Rahman
4 min read · Today

I didn’t need a perfect meal plan. I needed three tiny pauses between seeing the menu and saying my order.

For years, I ordered the same lunch without looking: white rice, extra gravy, sweet tea. It wasn’t “bad”—it was simply automatic. The change came when I stopped trying to reinvent lunch and started changing one detail at a time.

1. I chose before I reached the counter

On the walk over, I picked one intention: add a vegetable, choose water, or ask for sauce on the side. One decision was easier to remember than five rules.

2. I kept the food I actually liked

I still order chicken rice. Some days I choose brown rice; other days I simply add cucumber and skip the extra sauce. Familiar food makes a habit easier to repeat.

Try this today

Before your next meal out, choose just one swap. Post it to your circle before ordering—the tiny bit of accountability helps.

3. I celebrated the choice, not the calorie count

My circle reacted to every small win. That made the healthier choice feel social and positive, instead of like punishment.
